def factor_long_term_cycle_deviation(df):
    """Measure long-term cycle stage as normalized deviation of price from its 200-day SMA relative to 200-day ATR."""
    import pandas as pd
    import numpy as np
    df_copy = df.copy()
    # 200-day SMA
    sma200 = df_copy["close"].rolling(window=200, min_periods=1).mean()
    # True range
    high = df_copy["high"]
    low = df_copy["low"]
    close = df_copy["close"]
    tr_candidate1 = high - low
    tr_candidate2 = (high - close.shift(1)).abs()
    tr_candidate3 = (low - close.shift(1)).abs()
    true_range = pd.concat([tr_candidate1, tr_candidate2, tr_candidate3], axis=1).max(axis=1)
    atr200 = true_range.rolling(window=200, min_periods=1).mean()
    factor = (close - sma200) / atr200.replace(0.0, np.nan)
    df_copy["factor_long_term_cycle_deviation"] = factor
    return df_copy["factor_long_term_cycle_deviation"]
description: Captures where the current price sits relative to its long-term trend envelope in volatility-adjusted units. High positive values suggest overbought cyclical extremes, while low negatives indicate oversold extremes, reflecting phase within a long-term cycle.
